_comment: oc-l1 host-local config template (O1-LITE). Copy to the host-local location and fill in real values - a filled-in copy must NEVER be committed:
All values below are placeholders. 'password_env' is the NAME of the environment variable holding the Basic auth password - never a value.
Top-level keys are lane names; the 'name' field inside a lane must equal its key.

Optional keys with defaults: serve_port (stable hash of the lane name, 47200-47299), instructions ([AGENTS.md, handoff]), mcp ([autoos-agent]), plugins ([]), state_file (<scratch_dir>/oc-l1-<name>.state.json), scratch_dir (<tempdir>/autoos-oc-l1/<name>), canary_timeout_s (120), heartbeat_file (<scratch_dir>/heartbeat.json), workers_dir (<cwd>/logs/workers, pinned as AUTOOS_WORKERS_DIR for the autoos-agent MCP).
'plugins' must list the bash-guard plugin DIRECTORY: an unguarded lane has no plugin to deny the canary, so 'start' refuses it with exit 2 before spawning anything (D-665).

Orchestrator-lane keys (D-665, all optional, all absolute-path-free except where noted): 'permission' is a map of OpenCode permission key -> allow|deny|ask merged OVER the rendered defaults (e.g. {"task": "deny"} for a lane that must only coordinate); the reserved key 'external_directory' is refused there - it has its own lane list. 'guard_role' is exported to the server child as AUTOOS_GUARD_ROLE, and the bash-guard plugin's orchestrator role answers to it. 'inbox_file' is exported as AUTOOS_L1_INBOX - the file the lane's own REPORT/DONE lines are told to append to. 'first_prompt_file' is posted VERBATIM as the pilot's first prompt instead of the handoff head; 'start' refuses (exit 2) before spawning if it is named and missing.

All paths (cwd, handoff, opencode_bin, scratch_dir, state_file, plugins, instructions, heartbeat_file) must be absolute paths on the host that runs the config - opencode_bin must point at the explicit npm opencode binary, never a PATH-lookup name, never the desktop 'service'.
